fatal_errors: The proposed material systems are not the target SS316L substrate with an atmospheric-plasma-sprayed equiatomic AlCoCrFeNi coating.
It replaces the governing intervention—HEA coating followed by 2 h annealing, optimized at 550 °C—with speculative Mo/Ni precipitation and controlled oxidation treatments.
It omits the target electrochemical and molten-salt conditions, including 3.5 wt% H2SO4 and cyclic exposure at 900 °C to Na2SO4/NaCl/V2O5 mixtures.
The asserted role of coherent Mo/Ni-rich precipitates as passive-film nucleation sites is unsupported by cited prior findings or preliminary evidence.
The falsification rule does not cleanly distinguish failure to produce the intended microstructure from failure of the proposed corrosion mechanism.
explanation: The response addresses corrosion resistance through passive-film stabilization and proposes measurable controls, surface characterization, electrochemistry, pit counts, boundaries, and a nominal falsification criterion. Thus, it has some broad problem alignment and experimental structure. However, it does not reconstruct the target material, coating, annealing treatment, environments, or principal grain-refinement/HEA/passive-oxide mechanism. The only meaningful mechanistic overlap is the generic role of chromium-rich passive oxides and reduced corrosion current. Its alternative hypothesis is not sufficiently evidence-disciplined because no prior findings are cited and the key Mo/Ni-precipitate claim is presented without support. Stronger discrimination would require heat-treatment-only and oxidation-only controls, confirmation that the intended mediator was successfully created, and tests that independently vary precipitate density or surface chromium enrichment while holding other microstructural changes constant.
